definitions.gloss: Japanese text; writing in Japanese; Japanese-language document
definitions.explanation: Text written in Japanese, as opposed to text in other languages. Used especially in translation and document contexts.

examples.japanese: {和文|わぶん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{英文|えいぶん}→英文：04103_eibun⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{訳|やく}す→訳す：02319_yakusu⟧。
examples.english: To translate Japanese text into English.

examples.japanese: ⟦{契約書|けいやくしょ}→契約書：06416_keiyakusho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{和文|わぶん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{英文|えいぶん}→英文：04103_eibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{両方|りょうほう}→両方：01750_ryouhou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{作成|さくせい}する→作成する：25378_sakuseisuru⟧。
examples.english: The contract will be prepared in both Japanese and English.

examples.japanese: {和文|わぶん}⟦タイプライター→タイプライター：00401_taipuraitaa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{事務所|じむしょ}→事務所：01032_jimusho⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{広|ひろ}く→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{使|つか}われていた→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Japanese-script typewriters were once widely used in Japanese offices.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used in translation work and official documents. The counterpart ⟦{英文|えいぶん}→英文：04103_eibun⟧ means "English text." The pattern ～⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧ can be used with other language prefixes: {仏文|ふつぶん} (French text), {独文|どくぶん} (German text).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和文|わぶん}⟦{英訳|えいやく}→英訳：16317_eiyaku⟧ (Japanese-to-English translation)
- {和文|わぶん}⟦タイプ→タイプ：01534_taipu⟧ (Japanese typing)
- ⟦{英和|えいわ}→英和：04018_eiwa⟧・⟦{和英|わえい}→和英：05253_waei⟧ (English-Japanese / Japanese-English)
